inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 238,834,381 ordinary shares on issue (FY2025 annual report shareholder statistics) + 2.7m dilutive share/performance rights (note 6.2, FY2025 diluted WASO 241.2m). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge.
inputs.total_debt_note: core_metrics total_debt 32.9 = borrowings 19.3 + lease liabilities 13.6 (FY2025). Under lease treatment (B) only borrowings enter net debt.
inputs.net_debt_note: net_debt 16.3 = net bank debt NZ$5.8m at 30-Jun-2026 (H1 FY2026 result: borrowings less cash, EX-lease, management's own net-debt definition; FY2025 was net CASH 0.7m = 20.0 cash - 19.3 borrowings) + NZ$10.5m for non-controlling interests (FY2025 NCI profit share NZ$0.7m x 15; NCI book value only NZ$2.4m). NCI is charged ONCE, here in the bridge; the flows are 100% consolidated. Lease liabilities (13.6m) EXCLUDED because the full lease cash is deducted in the flows (treatment B).
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2026-06-30 (net bank debt, from H1 FY2026 results announcement via Analysis JSON); 2025-12-31 for all other balance-sheet items (FY2025 annual report -- the interim report PDF was not downloaded)
inputs.last_fcf_basis: Unlevered owner FCF FY2025 = OCF 27.8 + interest paid 2.1 - capex 21.1 - SBC 0.9 - interest income 0.1 - lease cash 6.8 (6.5 principal + 0.3 interest) = 1.0. Equivalent to reported FCF 6.7 - SBC 0.9 - interest income 0.1 - lease principal 6.5 + borrowing interest 1.8.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: OCF 27.8 - PPE 0.6 - capitalised software & intangibles 20.5 = 6.7 (company FCF definition, post-IFRS-16 so lease principal is NOT deducted).
inputs.capex_note: 20.5 of 21.1 is capitalised internally generated software (note 4.4) -- the cloud rebuild. It is charged as capex in every projected year.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report statement of changes in equity, share-based payments 0.9 (line 4107); history 0.5/5.2/4.5/3.2/1.8/0.9 FY20-FY25. No net-share-settlement tax line disclosed. Held at 0.5% of revenue rather than trended to zero -- LTI schemes continue.
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income NZ$0.1m FY2025. Deducted for completeness; immaterial and the company is now net debt, so no cash pile is being double-counted.
inputs.lease_treatment: B -- leases as operating cost. Full lease cash (principal + interest) charged inside the flows via lease_cost_pct_path (4.0% of revenue FY26, scaling down to 2.8% base); lease liabilities EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025: amortisation 15.9 + PPE depreciation 1.2 = 17.1 = 10.4% of revenue; ROU depreciation 4.4 excluded) so the lease is not charged twice.
inputs.buyback_note: No buybacks in any year FY2020-FY2025. The flat count is a modelling convention (SBC expensed), not something the company has paid for.
inputs.dividends_note: 0.4 paid to NCIs only; no ordinary dividend declared for FY2025 or H1 FY2026.
inputs.tax_losses_note: Deferred tax asset of NZ$28.5m recognised on NZ (28.2) and Netherlands (0.3) tax losses with no expiry, i.e. ~NZ$100m of gross losses; a further NZ$2.8m unrecognised. Cash taxes paid 0.3m FY2025 vs 1.8m P&L charge. Cash tax rate ramps 5% -> 28% (NZ statutory) by FY2033 rather than perpetuating the shelter.
inputs.guidance_fy2026: Revenue NZ$179-184m (raised 3-Aug-2026 from 176-182); EBITDA margin 18-20% (maintained); FCF neutral in H2 FY2026; 2030 exit-rate ARR aspiration NZ$315m; Vista Payments ARR >NZ$15m by 2030.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 11.5% NZD, identical across scenarios. Built from NZD flows: NZ 10-year government bond ~4.4% (Sep-2026) + beta ~1.2 x 5.5% ERP = 11.0%, plus ~0.5pp size/liquidity premium for a NZ$700m NZX/ASX small cap. Debt is <3% of EV so WACC ~ cost of equity. Cyclicality, cloud-execution and customer-concentration risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the rate (risk charged once).
inputs.market_implied_note: At NZ$2.91 the market cap is NZ$703m and ex-lease EV NZ$709m: 25x FY2025 EBITDA, 4.3x revenue, 4.2x ARR, and ~700x FY2025 owner FCF. The price is roughly the bull case with a 20x FCF exit at FY2030 discounted at ~11% -- i.e. it prices the NZ$315m 2030 ARR aspiration at a mature 30% margin as near-certain. The house model does not.
notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (dcf-methods SKILL routing: operating company, SaaS/software, non-US -> owner-fcf.md incl. section 7). Vista is a standard operating company; not a bank/REIT/LIC/holdco. First valuation of this ticker (no prior DCF, no memory entry).

Flow formula is the dashboard component engine's: EBIT = revenue x (EBITDA margin - SBC% - lease% - D&A%); cash tax on max(0, EBIT); FCF = EBIT - tax + D&A - capex + wc_capture x (revenue change). wc_capture +15%: deferred revenue (31.2m, up 5.3m in FY25) makes growth a modest cash inflow for this prepaid/subscription model.
10-year horizon because the owner-FCF margin is still ramping at year 5 (base 7.7% vs 10.8% mature); capitalising a 5-year margin would understate value.

FY2025 EBITDA 28.2 is the income-statement subtotal (post-IFRS-16, before capitalised development). Reported FCF (6.7) is NOT a steady state: FY2020-FY2024 reported FCF was negative every year and owner FCF (after lease and SBC) was negative in all six years until FY2025's +1.0m.

Year-1 (FY2026) owner FCF of NZ$1.4m (0.8% margin) is deliberately near zero: management guides FCF-neutral in H2 after an H1 swing to net debt, with capitalised software assumed at 14% of revenue while delivery capacity is added. The projection is still ~NZ$10m above what 'H1 negative + H2 neutral' would imply on a reported basis; the interim report was not available to reconcile further.

Historical CAGRs: revenue 3yr 6.7% / 5yr 13.4% (FY2020 is a COVID trough). EPS and owner-FCF CAGRs are undefined (negative start values). Equity CAGR is -1.5%/yr over 5 years (cumulative losses) and is NOT usable as the growth anchor; selected_growth_rate is the base-case FY26-FY30 revenue CAGR of 8.5%, anchored to FY2026 guidance and the ARR trajectory.
H1 FY2026 revenue 86.3m (+12.1%) and net loss -1.5m are consistent with the base year-1 path; not used as a run-rate (H2-weighted business).
Potentia/Admetus exited its 19.9% stake at NZ$3.00 in Sep-2025; Forsyth Barr target NZ$3.28 (May-2026). Both sit near the current price and far above house IV -- colour only, not a model input.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case FY2026-FY2030 revenue CAGR (guidance midpoint +10.5% FY26, decaying); equity CAGR unusable (loss-making transition), EPS/FCF CAGRs undefined from negative bases
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR -1.5% vs revenue 5yr CAGR 13.4%: equity shrank through FY2020-FY2024 losses while revenue grew. Equity CAGR rejected as the anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC - interest income - lease cash + finance costs as interest-paid proxy; FY2025 uses actual interest paid) was negative every year FY2020-FY2024 (-16.6, -9.0, -15.6, -18.6, -7.3) and +1.0 in FY2025. SBC fell from 5.2m (FY21) to 0.9m (FY25) so the owner-FCF trend is better than reported FCF's; the improvement is real but the level is still ~zero. ARR grew 11.4%/yr FY22-FY25.

base.narrative: Base: FY2026 lands at the guidance midpoint (revenue NZ$181.5m, +10.5%; EBITDA margin 18.0%, the low half of the 18-20% guide given H1's 13.8% FX-adjusted margin). Growth decays 10.5% -> 3.5% over ten years as the Vista Cloud migration (35% of sites at FY25; ODEON/AMC, Kinepolis, Cinepolis Mexico, Cineworld UK, Cinemex signed) lifts SaaS mix, but the 2030 ARR aspiration of NZ$315m is NOT reached (base revenue ~NZ$247m in FY2030). EBITDA margin expands 1pp/yr to 25.5% by FY2035 as onboarding costs are recovered and expensed R&D leverages. Capitalised software (12.5% of revenue in FY25, 14% assumed in FY26 while delivery capacity is being added) tapers to 8% by FY2034; D&A converges on capex with a lag. Lease cash (4.1% of revenue in FY25 after a new HQ lease) scales down to 2.8%. Cash tax shielded by NZ$28.5m of recognised deferred tax assets on ~NZ$100m of NZ losses, ramping from 5% to the 28% statutory rate by FY2033. Owner FCF goes from ~zero (FY25: NZ$1.0m) to ~10.8% of revenue at maturity.

bull.narrative: Bull: the cloud pipeline converts at pace and Vista Payments scales toward its NZ$15m+ ARR aspiration, so revenue compounds 12-13% through FY2029 and reaches ~NZ$292m in FY2030 (ARR run-rate ~NZ$315m, matching the stated 2030 aspiration). A strong 2026-27 slate (Avengers, Star Wars, Dune, Toy Story) lifts GTV-linked revenue. Operating leverage takes the EBITDA margin to 30% by FY2035 (vertical-SaaS peer territory), capitalised software falls to 7.5% of revenue and lease cost to 2.5%. Same tax ramp and WACC as base; terminal growth 3.5%.

bear.narrative: Bear: FY2026 comes in at the bottom of guidance (+8%), then a weak 2027-28 slate (as in the 2023 strike year) and a slower cloud delivery ramp hold growth at 2-4%; a major circuit renegotiates or churns (the Cinemex 2019 departure is the precedent). EBITDA margin stalls at 17-20% because the incremental delivery/technology spend is never fully recovered, capitalised software stays above 10% of revenue and lease cost stays at ~3.5%. Owner FCF is negative for three years and only reaches ~4% of revenue by FY2035; terminal growth 2.5%. Same WACC as base -- risk is charged in the flows, not the rate.

base.fcf_basis: Unlevered owner FCF: EBITDA - SBC - lease cash (principal+interest) - D&A ex-ROU = EBIT; cash tax on max(0,EBIT); + D&A - capex (incl. capitalised software) + wc_capture x revenue change. Lease liabilities therefore EXCLUDED from net debt (treatment B).

bull.fcf_basis: Unlevered owner FCF: EBITDA - SBC - lease cash (principal+interest) - D&A ex-ROU = EBIT; cash tax on max(0,EBIT); + D&A - capex (incl. capitalised software) + wc_capture x revenue change. Lease liabilities therefore EXCLUDED from net debt (treatment B).

bear.fcf_basis: Unlevered owner FCF: EBITDA - SBC - lease cash (principal+interest) - D&A ex-ROU = EBIT; cash tax on max(0,EBIT); + D&A - capex (incl. capitalised software) + wc_capture x revenue change. Lease liabilities therefore EXCLUDED from net debt (treatment B).

entry_price.method: Price at which the scenario's projected owner FCF over 10 years plus a terminal value BUILT AT THE 15% HURDLE (min(Gordon@15%, 18x FCF_10), re-capped at 15%) less net debt returns a 15% IRR. Per scenario, then probability-weighted.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at its own rate. 11.5% row = base intrinsic value; 15% row = base entry price.

sensitivity.note: Rows = WACC, columns = terminal growth. Base pair (11.5%, 3.0%) at the centre.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 20% bear / 50% base / 30% bull versus the 15/50/35 house default. Bear raised to 20%: profitability is thin (owner FCF ~zero after six loss years), the balance sheet swung to net debt in H1 FY2026 while the cloud migration is only 35% complete, and revenue is exposed to the film slate and to a handful of large circuits. Bull trimmed to 30%: it needs the cloud pipeline, Vista Payments AND the slate to all deliver together to reach the NZ$315m ARR aspiration. No going-concern or covenant risk (bank debt NZ$19m against NZ$28m EBITDA), so bear is not pushed to 30%+. Sums to 1.0.
probability_weighted.band_note: SBC is only 0.5% of revenue so the house/street band is narrow (NZ$0.97 house to NZ$1.03 street, weighted). The current price of NZ$2.91 sits far ABOVE the street ceiling (band position ~3,400%): the price is not explained by SBC treatment at all, it is explained by the market capitalising the 2030 ARR aspiration at a mature margin and a richer exit multiple than the house Gordon value grants.

valuation_summary.verdict: OVERVALUED on the house model in all three scenarios: even the bull case (NZ$1.68) is 42% below the NZ$2.91 price. Weighted IV NZ$0.97; weighted 15%-hurdle entry price NZ$0.59. The stock requires the bull path plus an exit multiple materially above the model's 12-13x owner FCF to justify today's price.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
